intro: Welcome, valued attendee, to the What?? panel: a free bonus session of the seminar. Every day the dice roll a premise and a dozen constraints, and the game has to honour all of them. Today's roll was seed 3133852973. Here is every roll, and what Tumble Hill made of it.

rolls.value: a wilted flower who only speaks in rhyme · recycling · kites
rolls.became: Tumble Hill is the windiest hill above Lowmarsh. The wind dried out the one flower on top, and the same wind drops every runaway kite in the valley on the hilltop, caked in mud. So the flower recycles them: scratch off the mud, sort the scrap, sell it.
Every word the flower says comes in couplets, from tear apologies to purchase speeches. Everyone else (the Exchange, the weather, the snail) talks in plain sentences.
Every kite arrives under a crust of mud. Drag across it like a scratch card to find out what it's made of: paper diamonds, silk deltas, box kites, ripstop stunt kites, dragon kites with gold thread.

The flower has turned being wilted into a brand. It runs a seminar called Wilt Your Way to Wealth, which nobody has ever attended, and buys itself an Affirmation Mirror, a Vision Board and a VIP Lanyard for its first VIP.
A broke guru is just a flower. The meter under the hill counts every dollar the Exchange has ever paid, all the way to seven figures.

The flower is wilted, so its petal droops and wobbles. Scratch too fast and it goes straight through the sail: every tear knocks the kite's grade down, and the scrap with it. Steady Stem (a lolly-stick splint, then a stake, then a posture coach) lets you scratch faster.

The Scrap Exchange. Prices drift up and down on their own, and since the flower is the only supplier, dumping a pile of silk sinks the price of silk. It climbs back while you wait, so you sell what's scarce and hold what's flooded. Advertising brings in more buyers.
Weather and sky over an exposed hill, arriving as old Mac alert boxes: gusts bring kites faster, drizzle brings the earthworms up, dew softens the mud, rumours and gluts move one price.

The game came out between the two peaks of the Taurid meteor showers, which are known for slow, bright fireballs. So one sky event is a slow fireball: all of Lowmarsh looks up and lets go of their strings, and six kites come in at once.
The Tramontane, the north wind that brings every kite to the hill. Also Tumble Hill, and the Tremendous.

Four growth spurts, from knee-high to cloud-high. Each one reaches kites that fly higher and are made of something better, and each new kite brings its own scrap to the Exchange. Earthworms keep scratching while you're away, and the mysterious buyer comes up the hill to buy what they cleaned.
Windows with striped title bars, rounded buttons, alert boxes with a warning sign, and a hill drawn in hard pixels and ordered dither. No anti-aliasing.
Five colours: purple ink on cream paper, pink for the flower and the kites' silk, mint for good prices and new leaves, thistle for the desktop and the mud.
Slow, airy pads in F lydian, a hilltop sky with the raised fourth for colour. More layers join as the stalk grows. Every scratch note and every sale chime is on the same scale.

Once you've earned a million and grown cloud-high, the Tramontane sends its last gale and the biggest kite in the valley: the Tremendous. Scratch it clean between gusts, and go gently while the wind blows.

rolls.value: it turns out someone asked for it
rolls.became: Every sale on the Exchange went to the same buyer, L.K.C., who pays in exact change and smells faintly of glue. Under the Tremendous's mud is a painted message: L.K.C. is the Lowmarsh Kite Club, who fly their old kites at the hill on purpose every year and buy the clean scrap back to build new ones. They asked for this. Then they come up the hill and fill the folding chairs.

outro: The flower would like you to know that it saw all of this coming, and that it's all in the workbook.
